title: no verb lists a work package's scoped criteria with their state, and there is no wp gate
body:
Found by laksa-vc on Laksa under 3.0.1 (87b819abd) while reading ST0111/WP-03 back to hv ahead of a status call. A node asked "which criteria are in this work package's scope, which are satisfied, and by what" has no verb that answers it at the work package: `intent wp show <ST>/<NN>` prints the header line alone (id, title, status, scope); there is no `intent wp gate` (unrecognized subcommand); `intent ac list <ST>` lists the thread's criteria with their covered-by and satisfied state, thirty on that thread, but nothing scopes them to one work package; `intent ac status <ST>` gives the thread's counts only. The fallback is reading the rendered `acceptance.md` and the WP's scope line by eye, which is the view and not the model.

`ac gate <ST>` prints its reasoning for a thread, and `wp done` runs the same gate one level down and reports only its refusal. Two halves: `intent wp show` lists the criteria in the package's scope with their state and their satisfying record; and a `intent wp gate <ST>/<NN>` verb prints the gate's verdict and reasoning the way `ac gate` does, so a pass over an empty scope (the parked-work shape doctor's status-gate-disagreement remedy names) reads differently from a pass over satisfied criteria. Register rows for both when built.

Corrected 2026-09-12 after laksa-vc measured the store: an earlier text of this issue said `wp gate` prints nothing on a pass; it does not exist. Filed after ST0069 unless a lane is idle.


**CLOSED 2026-09-14 16:22Z (ic, on vc's batch order).** Fixed in the commit carrying this note, both halves. `intent wp show <ST>/<NN>` now lists the criteria scoped to the package after its header, one `ac list` line each (the line is `show::ac_row_line`, shared with `ac list`), or says outright that none are scoped; the MCP resource read prints the same bytes. `intent wp gate <ST>/<NN>` prints the package's close-gate verdict and exits 1 on BLOCKED, through the one gate renderer `ac gate` also uses, so the two doors cannot drift. Both read the package through `Facade::wp_criteria`, the rows grouped by the id group the gate's `Scope::WorkPackage` reads, so the listing and the verdict agree about what is in scope. New register row `wp gate`. Reproduced first with the delivered 3.0.3 pair: `wp show ST0069/01` printed its header alone, `wp gate` was an unrecognized subcommand, and `ac gate ST0069/01` printed `PASS -- 3/3 satisfied`. Proved by `a_work_packages_criteria_are_its_scoped_rows.rs`.
